title: Normalized fraction arithmetic
instructions:
Implement `Fraction` in `fraction.py`, a small exact-rational value class.

## Files
- `fraction.py`

Public API (all arithmetic returns a new `Fraction`):
- `Fraction(numerator: int, denominator: int = 1)` stores public integer attributes
  `numerator` and `denominator`. Inputs must have exact type `int` (booleans are
  rejected with `TypeError`). A zero denominator raises `ValueError`.
- Always reduce by the greatest common divisor, put any minus sign on the numerator,
  and represent every zero as `0/1`.
- `add(other: Fraction) -> Fraction`, `subtract(other: Fraction) -> Fraction`, and
  `multiply(other: Fraction) -> Fraction` perform exact arithmetic without changing
  either operand. You may assume `other` is a `Fraction`.
- `as_tuple() -> tuple[int, int]` returns the normalized numerator and denominator.
- `str(fraction)` returns `"n/d"`, including `/1` for integers; no spaces.

Do not use `fractions.Fraction`. Python integers may be arbitrarily large.
